messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — new quantized reranker build (q5_0) passed local unit/eval harness but the prod holdout showed ~3.2% MRR drop after we enabled KV-pack caching :thinking_face:
arjun: can you paste the exact eval command + metric snippet?
maya: sure, ran locally and on canary: ```./eval_harness --model rw-rerank-3b --variant q5_0 --kvpack true --batch 64 --seed 42 --dataset holdout_v2 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr```
maya: local: MRR=0.452, NDCG@10=0.614  | canary (no kvpack): MRR=0.449, NDCG@10=0.610  | canary (kvpack on): MRR=0.435, NDCG@10=0.599
lin: interesting. kvpack effect that big is suspicious. did you change tokenization/preproc? even small whitespace/casing diffs can shift rerankers.
maya: preprocessing pipeline is same AFAIK: `normalize_unicode -> strip_html -> whitespace_collapse -> tokenizer.v1` but i did try a quick run where we concatenated doc fields with a single space vs newline — small diff in input formatting.
arjun: can you repro the gap in a deterministic single-run? i.e., same seed, same batching, and run kvpack on/off on the exact same saved candidate set.
maya: trying now. running seed sweep (42, 123, 7) and batch 1/16/64. started with seed 42.
eva: tagging in the eval ledger: https://redwood.internal/evals/ledger/4832 — added the canary job and raw outputs.
lin: also check the tokenizer subtok alignment at token boundaries — kvpack may be merging KV segments differently if we trim trailing spaces. earlier we saw off-by-one when doc ends with punctuation vs newline.
arjun: add this quick diff to reproduce: run pipeline producing T1 (join with ' ') and T2 (join with '\n'), then run quantized model q5_0 with kvpack true/false. if delta persists, dump debug KV keys for a handful of queries.
maya: did seed 42 batch64 run — results: kvpack=false MRR=0.450, kvpack=true MRR=0.436. seed 123 batch64: kv=false 0.451, kv=true 0.437
lin: consistent across seeds -> not random. suspect deterministic tokenization shift between how we serialize candidates into the KV cache vs eval harness. can you paste the serialized input for a failing example?
maya: pasted one failing example to the thread: ```QUERY: "how to set up k8s liveness"
CAND1: "...ensure /health returns 200.
etcd backup..."
SERIALIZED (kvpack=false): "how to set up k8s liveness 
 C: ensure /health returns 200. 
 etcd backup..."
SERIALIZED (kvpack=true): "how to set up k8s liveness
C: ensure /health returns 200.
etcd backup..."```
eva: small diff — extra spaces after sentence on one. can that shift positional embeddings?
lin: yes — rerankers are sensitive to early token alignment; quantized kernels + kvpack may change chunking and cause softmax differences. need to check exact token ids and segment boundaries.
arjun: request: add a debug step that dumps `token_ids` and `kv_chunk_boundaries` for the top 3 candidates where score flips. also compare logits before softmax.
maya: adding debug hook now and re-running on 50 failing queries. will upload artifacts to the eval run.
sre-bot: deploy canary update queued — canary id c-2023-338a — no rollback yet. :gear:
lin: other potential: integer quantization (q5_0) can amplify tiny input shifts. also check if we apply any post-token trimming when filling KV cache (we used to drop trailing newline but not spaces).
eva: i checked the commit history: `serve/kvpack` had a micro-change 2 days ago: "preserve trailing whitespace when serializing" (hash abc123). might explain it.
arjun: great catch. if kvpack now preserves trailing whitespace, that could create consistent token boundary shifts vs previous runs that collapsed trailing whitespace. revert that behavior for a quick test.
maya: test revert done on canary (kvpack revert -> preserve=false). rerun subset: kvpack with preserve=false MRR=0.448 (almost back). kvpack with preserve=true MRR=0.436.
lin: confirms hypothesis. plan: 1) keep preserve=false as safe default, 2) add regression test that compares token id sequences before and after serialization, 3) add a tolerance check in our eval harness for kvpack-enabled runs (alert if MRR delta > 0.5% vs baseline).
arjun: also file a tiny PR to make kv serialization explicitly normalized (strip trailing spaces, normalize newlines) and add a note in model onboarding guide about kvpack determinism.
maya: opened PR #5423 with norm change + unit tests. dropping a sample debug zip here: https://s3.redwood/internal/evals/canary-338-zip
eva: i've updated the eval ledger with the kvpack-preserve=false run as the new canary baseline.
sre-bot: canary c-2023-338a marked: degraded -> investigation flagged.
arjun: follow-ups: - add token-level dumps to failing-run alert - update onboarding checklist to include kvpack serialization check - run larger holdout sweep with preserve=false before promoting to prod
maya: agreed. i'll run 10k-holdout sweep overnight with preserve=false and attach summary tomorrow. thanks team :thumbsup:
lin: nice debugging! small string quirk cost us a lot of MRR. great find. :partyparrot:"
